title: MATH GAOKAO - 379
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a small positive integer power of \(i\).
questions.question: Compute \(i^{11}\).
questions.explanation:
Since \(i^4=1\),
\[
i^{11}=(i^4)^2i^3=i^2i=-i.
\]
The distractor has the wrong sign.
questions.hint: Reduce the exponent modulo four, then evaluate the remaining power.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a positive integer power of \(i\) that is a multiple of \(4\).
questions.question: Compute \(i^4\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a power of \(i\) whose exponent is congruent to \(2\) modulo \(4\).
questions.question: Compute \(i^6\).
questions.hint: Reduce the exponent modulo \(4\) and use \(i^2=-1\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a power of \(i\) whose exponent is congruent to \(1\) modulo \(4\).
questions.question: Compute \(i^9\).
questions.hint: Use \(i^4=1\) and write the exponent as a multiple of \(4\) plus a remainder.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a power of \(i\) whose exponent is congruent to \(2\) modulo \(4\).
questions.question: Compute \(i^{18}\).
questions.hint: Divide the exponent by \(4\) and use the remainder.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a sum of two large powers of \(i\) using modular arithmetic.
questions.question: Compute \(i^{2023}+i^{2024}\).
questions.hint: Reduce each exponent modulo \(4\) before adding.

questions.concept: Sum of a Complete Cycle of Powers of \(i\)
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate the sum of four consecutive powers of \(i\) forming one complete cycle.
questions.question: Evaluate \(1+i+i^2+i^3\).
questions.hint: Write each power in terms of \(1\), \(i\), \(-1\), and \(-i\).

questions.concept: Negative Powers of the Imaginary Unit
questions.learningObjective: Compute the reciprocal of \(i\) using the fact that \(i^{-1}=-i\).
questions.question: Compute \(i^{-1}\).
questions.explanation:
Since \[
\begin{aligned}
i\cdot(-i)&=-i^2 \\
&=-(-1) \\
&=1
\end{aligned}
\], the reciprocal of \(i\) is \(-i\). Equivalently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
i^{-1}&=\frac{1}{i} \\
&=\frac{1}{i}\cdot\frac{-i}{-i} \\
&=\frac{-i}{-i^2} \\
&=\frac{-i}{1} \\
&=-i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(i^{-1}=-i\).
questions.hint: Find a complex number whose product with \(i\) equals \(1\).

questions.learningObjective: Simplify an expression involving products of powers of \(i\).
questions.question: Compute \((i^5+i^6)(i^7+i^8)\).
questions.explanation:
Reduce each power modulo \(4\):
\[
i^5=i,\quad i^6=-1,\quad i^7=-i,\quad i^8=1.
\]
Then
\[
i^5+i^6=i-1,\qquad i^7+i^8=1-i.
\]
Their product is
\[
\begin{aligned}
(i-1)(1-i)&=i-i^2-1+i \\
&=i+1-1+i \\
&=2i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the value is \(2i\).
questions.hint: First simplify each power of \(i\), then multiply the two resulting complex numbers.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a long sum of powers of \(i\) by grouping complete cycles.
questions.question: Find \(\displaystyle \sum_{k=1}^{2023} i^k\).
questions.explanation:
The powers of \(i\) repeat in cycles of length \(4\), and each complete cycle satisfies
\[
i+i^2+i^3+i^4=i-1-i+1=0.
\]
Since
\[
2023=4\cdot 505+3,
\]
the first \(2020\) terms form \(505\) complete cycles and contribute \(0\). The remaining three terms are
\[
i^{2021}+i^{2022}+i^{2023}=i-1-i=-1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{2023} i^k=-1.
\]
questions.hint: Group the terms into blocks of four consecutive powers of \(i\).
